evidence.author: milliedabostonterrier
evidence.raw_text: So wonderful you are making fresh food for your dog. But this should only be once in a while as it is not balanced. Over time, even with the synthetic supplement, your beautiful dog will have issues, and it's a big breed - so important to get it balanced. Also, no need for crock pot, you are cooking out so many vitamins. Rice is not a food for dogs - unless they have tunny issues, then use it for a Congee only. There is hardly any meat in this and missing calcium for their bones. Fatty fish for there well being, coat and skin. Heart - for their heart . Liver, is vital. And one other secreting organ. Feed 2-3% of their correct body weight. Guideline: 65% muscle meat, 5% liver from any animal/poultry, 5% other secreting organ, 25% veggie mix - steamed, cooked, mashed (a must). Those are the guidelines for a lightly cooked meal. Raw is different, but also wonderful. 3-4 different proteins for batch of food. 1/2 teasp. ground powdered eggshells per pound of food. Fatty fish as a topper a few times per week, egg too. Rotating proteins/organs is important. Each protein has a different nutritional profile. Introduce everything slow - to make sure it all agrees with your dog, especially the organs - they are rich. Heart is important to put in every meal, no more than 10% of the protein. Heart from beef, pork, lamb, chicken etc. Good luck. Great nutrition equals hardly any Vet bills. Unbalanced food for too long = a Vet's dream.
